description: We are a PlutonyX Team, working hard to win.
summary: Plutonyx is an interactive space mission game that puts players in the role of mission control. Space exploration is often experienced through passive videos or complex data charts, which can make it feel distant. We created Plutonyx in two ways: an instant browser version with no installation required, and an installable app version that offers improved graphics over the web edition. Players launch missions, face space challenges, and make operational decisions in real time. With the limited time and resources we had during the hackathon, we focused on delivering a working, playable experience that makes space exploration engaging and accessible for everyone.
details:
What It Does & How It Works
PROJECT JEZERO is a story-driven Mars survival game. Players command a small outpost in Jezero Crater and must keep their crew alive while balancing air, power and radiation shielding, with food, water and a long signal delay to Earth adding hard trade-offs. Every choice costs something. Solar storms in the game come from real NASA DONKI space-weather data, radiation levels are based on NASA RadLab dosimetry data, and the terrain comes from real NASA Mars data. Each ending explains the real science behind what happened. We created two versions so anyone can play: an instant browser version that runs with zero installation, and an installable app version that offers better graphics than the web edition.

Benefits & Intended Impact
Space exploration and mission operations often feel distant or overly technical for everyday people. By turning mission planning and problem-solving into an active game, Plutonyx makes space concepts easier to understand and more engaging. Our intended impact is to give students, educators, and space enthusiasts a simple, hands-on way to experience how space missions work and spark deeper interest in space science.

How Our Project Is Creative
Rather than presenting space information as static text or passive slides, we designed Plutonyx around active decision-making—letting players directly experience the tension and trade-offs of running a mission. Offering both an instant-access browser version and an upgraded-graphics installable app also lets players choose between quick convenience and a richer visual experience.

Tools, Coding Languages, Hardware & Software Used

  • Web & App Development: TypeScript, Three.js and Vite for the web edition; Unity and Blender for the desktop edition and 3D assets.
  • Hosting & Collaboration: Git and GitHub for collaboration; the web edition is hosted on Vercel.
  • Hardware: Built and tested on our team's standard personal laptops.
  • AI Assistance: AI tools were used to assist with brainstorming, troubleshooting, text editing, and demo preparation.

Factors Our Team Considered
Working with limited time and resources during the hackathon, our five-person team focused on delivering the strongest, most reliable version we could:

  • Accessibility: Making sure anyone—including judges and students on basic laptops—can launch and test the browser version immediately without downloading anything.
  • Visual Quality vs. Performance: Creating a separate installable app version so we could deliver improved graphics without slowing down the web build.
  • Realistic Scope: Focusing on a working, playable core experience rather than overpromising unfinished features.
